setupSteps: Choose the version for today. Default for everyone new: step-back, no push-up, no jump. Use the incline version if you have wrist, shoulder or weight concerns, or find the plank too hard. Use the full burpee only if you have done step-back burpees comfortably for at least 2-3 weeks and have no neighbours below (est.).

Pick the floor. A flat floor with no loose rug. Put a non-slip yoga mat (6 mm or thicker, est.) down; the mat must not slide when your hands or feet land. No polished marble or wet tiles; no socks on smooth floors (bare feet or grip shoes).

Incline setup. Put a sturdy bench, heavy table or counter edge against a wall so it cannot slide. Press down on it with both hands, hard; it must not rock or tip. Avoid chairs with wheels, folding or plastic garden chairs, and anything on a polished floor that can slip. The hands go on the flat, firm top edge.

Clear the space. About 2 m of floor lengthways, nothing under you (shoes, bottles, dumbbells), a clear area beside you, and a ceiling fan switched off or well above you if you stand up with an overhead reach.
Stance. Stand tall, feet hip-width apart, toes pointing forward or slightly out, knees soft, arms by your sides.
Hand position (floor). In the plank, hands on the mat directly under the shoulders, fingers spread and pointing forward, with your weight spread over the whole palm (not only the heel of the hand).
Foot position in the plank. Feet hip-width apart, toes tucked under, a straight line from head to heels.
Neighbour rule. Place, don't drop. Lower hands and feet onto the mat with control. Do not kick the feet back, and do not jump. Keep the sound down even in the step-back version (est.).
Camera. Phone in landscape at hip height (about 80-100 cm, est.), about 2.5 m to your side (the plank is about 1.7 m long, est.), whole body visible from your fingertips to your head in the plank.
Clothing. Fitted leggings or track pants and a fitted top so the camera can see hips and knees.
Warm up for 2 minutes: march on the spot, arm circles, 5 bodyweight squats (Home 1), a few slow cat-camel or hip circles on the mat; nothing high-impact.

steps.part: A. Beginner step-back burpee (no jump, no push-up)
steps.title: Stand tall
steps.action: Feet hip-width apart, arms by your sides, eyes forward.
steps.feel: Even weight on both feet; calm, upright.
steps.visualCheck: Side: ear, shoulder, hip and ankle roughly in one vertical line. Front: shoulders and hips level.

steps.part: A. Beginner step-back burpee (no jump, no push-up)
steps.title: Sit your hips back and bend the knees
steps.action: Push the hips back and down as in a squat until your hands can reach the mat. Keep the chest lifted and the heels down.
steps.feel: Thighs and bottom loading; back long.
steps.visualCheck: Side: back straight and tilted forward, not rounded; knees over the toes. Front: knees over the second toes, not caving in.

steps.part: A. Beginner step-back burpee (no jump, no push-up)
steps.title: Place both hands on the mat
steps.action: Reach forward and place both palms flat on the mat, shoulder-width apart, just in front of your feet. Do not drop the weight onto them.
steps.feel: Weight going gently into the whole palm, shoulders stacked over hands as you lean.
steps.visualCheck: Side: wrists under or just in front of the shoulders. Front: hands shoulder-width apart, fingers pointing forward.

steps.part: A. Beginner step-back burpee (no jump, no push-up)
steps.title: Step the right foot back
steps.action: Transfer weight onto the hands and left foot, lift the right foot and step it straight back into the plank, toes tucked under.
steps.feel: Weight moving to the arms; trunk firm.
steps.visualCheck: Side: right leg straight, hip not high. Front: hips level, no twisting.

steps.part: A. Beginner step-back burpee (no jump, no push-up)
steps.title: Step the left foot back to meet it
steps.action: Step the left foot back beside the right so both feet are hip-width apart in a high plank.
steps.feel: Belly firm, shoulders over hands, bottom lightly squeezed.
steps.visualCheck: Side: one straight line from ear through shoulder and hip to ankle, no sag, no pike. Front: elbows straight but not locked hard.

steps.part: A. Beginner step-back burpee (no jump, no push-up)
steps.title: Hold the plank for one breath
steps.action: Press the floor away from you and hold still for one slow breath.
steps.feel: Trunk and shoulders working; wrists comfortable.
steps.breathing: One full breath: in, then out.
steps.visualCheck: Side: straight line; neck long, eyes looking at the floor just ahead of your hands.

steps.part: A. Beginner step-back burpee (no jump, no push-up)
steps.title: Step the right foot forward
steps.action: Step the right foot forward outside the right hand, so the foot lands softly on the mat.
steps.feel: The thigh and trunk take the weight again.
steps.visualCheck: Side: foot lands under or just behind the hand line. Front: knee tracks over the toes.

steps.part: A. Beginner step-back burpee (no jump, no push-up)
steps.title: Step the left foot forward
steps.action: Step the left foot forward so both feet are back near the hands in the squat position.
steps.feel: Weight back through the heels, chest lifting.
steps.visualCheck: Side: back not rounded; hips low. Front: feet hip-width apart.

steps.part: A. Beginner step-back burpee (no jump, no push-up)
steps.title: Stand up tall
steps.action: Press through both heels and midfoot, bring the chest up and straighten the hips and knees. Do not jump. Finish with the hips fully tall.
steps.feel: Thighs and bottom working, then relaxed.
steps.visualCheck: Side: knees and hips almost straight (about 165 degrees or more, est.); torso upright. Front: hips and shoulders level.

steps.part: A. Beginner step-back burpee (no jump, no push-up)
steps.title: Rest and repeat
steps.action: Take one calm breath, then repeat from step 2. Rest 45-60 s after each set (3 to 5 reps).
steps.feel: Warm, breathing a bit faster but able to speak in sentences.
steps.breathing: One full breath between reps for the first sets.
steps.visualCheck: The last rep looks like the first: no sag, no rounded back, quiet steps.

steps.part: B. Incline burpee (hands on a bench or counter; the easiest version)
steps.title: Stand facing the bench or counter, about one foot-length (20-30 cm, est.) away. Hinge at the hips and bend the knees slightly, and place both hands on the firm top edge, shoulder-width apart

steps.part: B. Incline burpee (hands on a bench or counter; the easiest version)
steps.title: Step the right foot back, then the left, until the body is one straight line from head to heels on a slope (hands on the bench). Hold for one breath with the belly firm

steps.part: B. Incline burpee (hands on a bench or counter; the easiest version)
steps.title: Step the right foot forward, then the left foot, back toward the bench. Bring the chest up and stand tall (no jump). Start with the bench at hand height of about 60-90 cm (est.) and lower it step by step toward the floor as it gets easy. The higher the surface, the easier the move

commonMistakes.title: Hips sagging in the plank
commonMistakes.text: Hips sagging in the plank. Why: the lower back arches and takes the load instead of the trunk muscles; this is the most common fault noted by trainers and by a physical therapist quoted in one of the sources. Fix: squeeze the bottom, firm the belly, shorten the hold, or raise the hands on a bench (incline version).

commonMistakes.title: Kicking or jumping the feet back, or dropping onto the hands
commonMistakes.text: Kicking or jumping the feet back, or dropping onto the hands. Why: it is loud for the flat below, jars the wrists, shoulders and back, and gives no control. Fix: step one foot at a time and place hands softly; this is the default FitPlate version.

commonMistakes.title: Jumping and landing stiff-legged
commonMistakes.text: Jumping and landing stiff-legged. Why: the jump and landing add impact to the knees, hips and back and are loud in a flat. Fix: no jump at all for beginners; if progressing, land on the mat with bent knees and only if there are no neighbours below.

commonMistakes.title: Hands too far forward or too wide
commonMistakes.text: Hands too far forward or too wide. Why: puts strain on the wrists, neck and shoulders. Fix: hands directly under the shoulders, shoulder-width apart.

commonMistakes.title: Rounding the back or collapsing in the squat
commonMistakes.text: Rounding the back or collapsing in the squat. Why: rounds the lower back as you reach for the floor. Fix: send the hips back, lift the chest and keep the back long, or use the incline version so you do not have to fold as far.

commonMistakes.title: Rushing to chase the heart rate
commonMistakes.text: Rushing to chase the heart rate. Why: sloppy form, breath holding and dizziness; beginners often go too fast too early. Fix: one calm breath between reps in the first sessions, stop each set with 2-3 reps still in the tank, rest 45-60 s.

commonMistakes.title: Holding the breath
commonMistakes.text: Holding the breath. Why: raises blood pressure during effort (breathing study PubMed 7741618, carried from earlier items). Fix: breathe out as you stand or push, in as you step or sink.

commonMistakes.title: Letting the head drop or crane
commonMistakes.text: Letting the head drop or crane. Why: strains the neck and spoils the straight line. Fix: look at the floor a hand-length ahead of the fingertips in the plank.

commonMistakes.title: Knees caving in the squat or stand-up
commonMistakes.text: Knees caving in the squat or stand-up. Why: more stress on the knee; coaching and clinical sources link it to knee pain (mechanism inferred; burpee-specific trial: Not found). Fix: push knees out over the second toe; slow down.

commonMistakes.title: Doing too many too soon
commonMistakes.text: Doing too many too soon. Why: delayed soreness, wrist and shoulder overuse, and injury; sources suggest beginners start with a handful of reps. Fix: 3 x 5 step-back burpees, 2-3 days a week, add one thing at a time.

safetyNotes: Wrist problems (desk workers, carpal tunnel, past sprain): wrist pain with push-ups and burpees is one of the most common complaints physical therapists hear from patients (a military-base article by a physical therapy student, snippet only). Use fists on the mat, push-up handles, or the incline version with the hands on a bench; keep the wrist straight if it hurts when bent back.

Lower back pain: the plank is where the lower back takes load when the hips sag (a physical therapist quoted by one source). Use the incline version, shorten the hold and brace the belly; avoid the full burpee while pain is present.
Knee, hip, ankle problems: the jump is the part that aggravates these (sources). Use the no-jump step-back or incline version, a shallower squat and a mat; avoid deep squats if the knees hurt.
Shoulder problems: the plank loads the shoulders; use the incline version, shorten the plank or skip to standing squat plus wall push-ups.

High blood pressure and heart disease: burpees can push heart rate and blood pressure up quickly. HIIT sources list uncontrolled high blood pressure (for example above 180/110) and diagnosed heart disease as reasons to get medical clearance first; breathe out on effort; use the slow beginner version only after clearance.
Pregnancy and postpartum: ask your obstetrician or a women's health physiotherapist; jumping can strain the pelvic floor and balance changes.

Osteoporosis: low-level jumping may be fine in some people but people with spinal osteoporosis or a past spine fracture are advised to keep impact low and avoid repeated or loaded spine bending; use the step-back or incline version, keep the spine long and ask your doctor.
Dizziness or breathlessness: this move gets the heart going fast; use long rests and stop if you feel faint.

Floor and neighbours (Mumbai flat): use a thick, non-slip mat, no jumping, no kick-backs, do not do burpees early in the morning or late at night over a bedroom below (est.), and avoid hard tiles without a mat.

conditionCautions.change: Incline version; brace the belly; stop the plank hold when hips sag; avoid the full burpee while pain is present; stop if pain spreads down a leg
conditionCautions.source: Physical therapist quoted on plank arching (snippet); burpee-specific clinical guidance Not found

conditionCautions.change: Incline version at a high surface or skip the plank; avoid push-up versions; stop with pinching or sharp pain; get a diagnosis for persistent pain
conditionCautions.source: Wrist and shoulder push-up modification guides (blogs, snippets); clinical burpee-specific advice Not found

conditionCautions.change: No jump; low impact; keep the spine long, avoid repeated or loaded forward bending; low-level jumping is a case-by-case clinical choice for those without spine fractures
conditionCautions.source: RACGP osteoporosis exercise guidance (snippet); Society for Endocrinology Strong, Steady, Straight quick guide (snippet); Brooke-Wavell et al. 2022 (carried)

conditionCautions.change: Ask your obstetrician; if cleared, drop the jump and push-up and use step-back or incline with long rests; stop for bleeding, pain, dizziness or contractions
conditionCautions.source: Babylist physical therapist advice (secondary); KidsHealth high-impact pregnancy article (snippet); ACOG's own wording Not found; Mayo Clinic pregnancy exercises (carried)

conditionCautions.change: Ask a women's health physiotherapist first; jumping and burpees are high-impact and a return-to-running guideline suggests waiting at least about 12 weeks and being free of pelvic floor symptoms; stop for leaking, heaviness or belly doming
conditionCautions.source: Goom, Donnelly and Brockwell 2019 via secondary summaries (snippets); NHS Lothian DRAMs guidelines (carried)

conditionCautions.change: Only with surgeon or physiotherapist approval, especially after abdominal, spine, shoulder, knee, hip or ankle surgery
